practices.practice: Create one MongoClient per process (singleton) and reuse it across requests rather than constructing a new client per request.

Tune and size the MongoDB connection pool per environment (small maxPoolSize for serverless; larger pools for long-running OLTP servers) and initialize the client outside request handlers so the pool is reused.

Keep credentials out of source control: read connection strings from the environment (or a secrets manager) and prefer Microsoft Entra ID / Key Vault for production secrets rather than embedding passwords in code.
Always use TLS for connections to Azure DocumentDB and use SCRAM‑SHA‑256 as the supported MongoDB auth mechanism; do not disable certificate verification in production.

Store embeddings in a dedicated numeric field (e.g., embedding) and store fixed-dimension metadata (model name, dimensions, version) and other metadata (id, source, created_at) in separate indexed fields to support filtering and provenance.

Ensure the vector index's declared dimensions exactly match the embedding dimensionality and validate embedding length at write time so mismatched dimensions do not silently produce incorrect results.

practices.practice: When using cosine similarity, L2-normalize vectors at ingest (unit length) and store the embedding model name and dimensions with each vector so you can detect model drift and reindex if the model changes.

Pick the vector index type appropriate to scale (vector-ivf for <10k, vector-hnsw up to ~50k, prefer vector-diskann for production large-scale workloads) and tune index parameters such as maxDegree, lBuild (DiskANN) or m and efConstruction (HNSW) to trade build time, recall and memory.

practices.practice: Run vector-index creation and heavy index builds in the background or during a maintenance window (or use blocking on empty collections), and monitor build progress (db.currentOp) to avoid impacting production traffic.

Use the $search aggregation stage with operator cosmosSearch to run k‑NN queries, tune k and lSearch (or efSearch/efSearch depending on algorithm) for the recall/latency tradeoff, and use the internal filter clause to prefilter candidates rather than post-filtering.

Create regular (non-vector) indexes on fields you plan to filter by (customer_id, type, date, language, etc.) so you can supply those predicates to the vector search's filter field and reduce the candidate set efficiently.

When ingesting many documents (seeding or backfills) use bulk/batched writes (insertMany/bulkWrite) and chunk loads into appropriately sized batches to reduce roundtrips and improve throughput; Azure DocumentDB supports large bulk batch sizes but observe per-batch limits and tune for the cluster.
Implement retries with exponential backoff and jitter for transient network and rate-limit errors (e.g., 429), and design bulk/index operations to be idempotent or track progress so retries are safe.

Treat embeddings and vector indexes as sensitive data: encrypt in transit and at rest, restrict network access with private endpoints and firewall rules, and apply strict access control rather than exposing raw embeddings to clients.

practices.practice: Store the embedding model name and version together with each vector so you can detect model changes and reindex when switching embedding models.

Limit per-request result sizes (top‑k) on the server, select and de-duplicate retrieved passages, and assemble/truncate prompt context server-side to meet LLM token budgets before sending to the model.

practices.practice: Use projection to exclude very large text or binary fields from queries and, when appropriate, store large content in a side collection keyed by document id to reduce I/O and network costs.
Use TTL indexes (expireAfterSeconds) for ephemeral collections but ensure the indexed field is a Date, understand coarse (~60s) expiry cadence, and don't rely on TTL for precise deletion timing.
Enable diagnostic settings and slow-query logging, export logs to Log Analytics, use explain('executionStats') to find COLLSCANs and tune indexes or provisioning based on metrics and alerts.

Follow a safe index lifecycle: inventory indexes and usage ($indexStats), hide an index to test effects, monitor for regressions, then drop it off-peak; use blocking/create-on-empty when you need index to exist before writes.

When building RAG, sanitize and de-duplicate retrieved passages, prefer top-k selection and relevance thresholds, and consider summarization to keep prompts within model token budgets and reduce hallucination risk.
Prefer least-privilege credentials and Microsoft Entra ID / RBAC for production apps; give service accounts only the permissions needed for their operations and rotate credentials regularly.
When using DiskANN, tune maxDegree and lBuild at index creation and tune lSearch at query time (ensure lSearch >= k) to trade memory, build time and recall appropriately.
Use the $meta: 'searchScore' projection to return scores and project only the minimal fields you need (ids, score, small metadata) instead of full documents to reduce network and token costs.
Consider half-precision (fp16) or product quantization to reduce vector index memory footprint when appropriate, and A/B test recall before and after compression.
Use explain('executionStats') or MCP explain tools to inspect query plans, totalKeysExamined/totalDocsExamined and confirm new indexes actually remove COLLSCANs.

For serverless functions initialize the MongoClient outside the function handler and use small pool sizes (e.g., maxPoolSize 3–5) and low minPoolSize so warm invocations can reuse connections efficiently.
When changing embedding models or normalization strategy bump embedding version metadata and run a reindex/backfill under maintenance so index and stored vectors remain consistent.
